G4778.d: from σύν and κακουχέω; to maltreat in company with, i.e. (passively) endure persecution together:--suffer affliction with.

G4885.d: from σύν and αὐξάνω; to increase (grow up) together:--grow together.

G4678.d: from σοφός; wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual):--wisdom.

G4754.d: middle voice from the base of στρατιά; to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations:--soldier, (go to) war(-fare).

G4587.d: from σεμνός; venerableness, i.e. probity:--gravity, honesty.

G4954.d: from σύν and σῶμα; of a joint body, i.e. (figuratively) a fellow-member of the Christian community:--of the same body.

G4510.d: from ῥύπος; to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally):--be filthy.

G4932.d: from σύν and the base of τομώτερος; to contract by cutting, i.e. (figuratively) do concisely (speedily):--(cut) short.

G4512.d: from ῥύομαι; a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on the face):--wrinkle.

G4658.d: probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage:--Scythian.

G4881.d: from σύν and ἀπόλλυμι; to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with:--perish with.

G4532.d: of Hebrew origin (שָׁלֵם); Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine:--Salem.

G4628.d: apparently from (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank):--leg.

G4624.d: from σκάνδαλον; to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure):--(make to) offend.

G4908.d: from συνίημι; mentally put (or putting) together, i.e. sagacious:--prudent. Compare φρόνιμος.

G4737.d: from στέφανος; to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively):--crown.

G4755.d: from the base of στρατιά and ἄγω or ἡγέομαι; a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (prætor), the chief (præfect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens:--captain, magistrate.

G4854.d: from σύν and a derivative of φύω; grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to:--planted together.

G4577.d: probably from σύρω through its congener (to fasten; akin to αἱρέομαι); a chain (as binding or drawing):--chain.

G4645.d: from σκληρός; to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn:--harden.

G4550.d: from σήπω; rotten, i.e. worthless (literally or morally):--bad, corrupt. Compare πονηρός.

G4849.d: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of συμπίνω; a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests:--company.

G4695.d: from σπίλος; to stain or soil (literally or figuratively):--defile, spot.

G4752.d: from στρατεύομαι; military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger):--warfare.

G4833.d: from σύμμορφος; to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate:--make conformable unto.

G4861.d: from σύν and ψυχή; co-spirited, i.e. similar in sentiment:--like-minded.

G4975.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of ἔχω as adverb; nigh, i.e. nearly:--almost.

G4609.d: contraction for Σιλουανός; Silas, a Christian:--Silas.

G4667.d: the same as σμύρνα; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor:--Smyrna.

G4896.d: from σύν and (to go); to assemble:--gather together.

G4546.d: of Hebrew origin (שִׁמְשׁוֹן); Sampson (i.e. Shimshon), an Israelite:--Samson.

G4631.d: from σκεῦος; furniture, i.e. spare tackle:--tackling.

G4995.d: from σωφρονίζω; discipline, i.e. self-control:--sound mind.

G4728.d: probably from the base of ἵστημι; narrow (from obstacles standing close about):--strait.

G4960.d: from σύν and στοιχέω; to file together (as soldiers in ranks), i.e. (figuratively) to correspond to:--answer to.

G4747.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of στοιχέω; something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively):--element, principle, rudiment.

G4879.d: from σύν and ἀπάγω; to take off together, i.e. transport with (seduce, passively, yield):--carry (lead) away with, condescend.

G4831.d: from a presumed compound of σύν and μιμέομαι; a co-imitator, i.e. fellow votary:--follower together.

G4978.d: from σχίζω; a split or gap ("schism"), literally or figuratively:--division, rent, schism.

G4874.d: from σύν and a compound of ἀνά and μίγνυμι; to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with:--(have, keep) company (with).

G4819.d: from σύν and the base of βάσις; to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. concur (take place):--be(-fall), happen (unto).

G4733.d: from στερεόω; something established, i.e. (abstractly) confirmation (stability):--stedfastness.

G4623.d: from (silence, i.e. a hush; properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from σιγή, which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like 2974 properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water):--dumb, (hold) peace.

G4526.d: of Hebrew origin (שַׂק); "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief):-- sackcloth.

G4815.d: from σύν and λαμβάνω; to clasp, i.e. seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid:--catch, conceive, help, take.

G4993.d: from σώφρων; to be of sound mind, i.e. sane, (figuratively) moderate:--be in right mind, be sober (minded), soberly.

G4791.d: from σύν and κοινωνός; a co-participant:--companion, partake(-r, -r with).

G4992.d: neuter of the same as σωτηρία as (properly, concretely) noun; defender or (by implication) defence:--salvation.

G4794.d: from σύν and κύπτω; to stoop altogether, i.e. be completely overcome by:--bow together.

G4732.d: from στερεός; to solidify, i.e. confirm (literally or figuratively):--establish, receive strength, make strong.

G4839.d: from σύν and παραμένω; to remain in company, i.e. still live:--continue with.

G4525.d: akin to σείω; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb):--move.

G4977.d: apparently a primary verb; to split or sever (literally or figuratively):--break, divide, open, rend, make a rent.

G4957.d: from σύν and σταυρόω; to impale in company with (literally or figuratively):--crucify with.

G4581.d: from (Seleucus, a Syrian king); Seleuceia, a place in Syria:--Seleucia.

G4988.d: from the base of σώζω and that of σθενόω; of safe strength; Sosthenes, a Christian:--Sosthenes.

G4972.d: from σφραγίς; to stamp (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication, to keep secret, to attest:--(set a, set to) seal up, stop.

G4803.d: from συζητέω; mutual questioning, i.e. discussion:--disputation(-ting), reasoning.

G4966.d: of Hebrew origin (שְׁכֶם); Sychem (i.e. Shekem), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine:--Sychem.

G4979.d: diminutive of (a rush or flag-plant; of uncertain derivation); a rushlet, i.e. grass-withe or tie (generally):--small cord, rope.

G4799.d: from συγχέω; commixture, i.e. (figuratively) riotous disturbance:--confusion.

G4822.d: from σύν and (to force; causative (by reduplication) of the base of βάσις); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach:--compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove.

G4711.d: from σπείρω (as woven); a hamper or lunch-receptacle:--basket.

G4934.d: middle voice from σύν and τίθημι; to place jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to consent (bargain, stipulate), concur:--agree, assent, covenant.

G4913.d: middle voice from σύν and the base of ἡδονή; to rejoice in with oneself, i.e. feel satisfaction concerning:--delight.

G4850.d: from σύν and πρεσβύτερος; a co-presbyter:--presbyter, also an elder.

G4718.d: probably from the base of στέφανος; a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined):--grapes.

G4537.d: from σάλπιγξ; to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively):--(which are yet to) sound (a trumpet).

G4824.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of σύμβουλος; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court:--consultation, counsel, council.

G4951.d: probably akin to αἱρέομαι; to trail:--drag, draw, hale.

G4980.d: from σχολή; to take a holiday, i.e. be at leisure for (by implication, devote oneself wholly to); figuratively, to be vacant (of a house):--empty, give self.

G4506.d: middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to ῥέω (through the idea of a current; compare ῥύσις); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. rescue:--deliver(-er).

G4875.d: middle from σύν and ἀναπαύω; to recruit oneself in company with:--refresh with.

G4599.d: from (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of ἵστημι); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power):--strengthen.

G4555.d: from the same as σάρδιος; sardine (λίθος being implied), i.e. a gem, so called:--sardine.

G4760.d: from the base of στρατιά and the same as πεδινός; a camping-ground, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops:--army.

G4998.d: from the base of σώζω and that of φρήν; safe (sound) in mind, i.e. self-controlled (moderate as to opinion or passion):--discreet, sober, temperate.

G4501.d: probably of foreign origin; a sabre, i.e. a long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively):--sword.

G4514.d: from Ῥώμη; Romæan, i.e. Roman (as noun):--Roman, of Rome.

G4793.d: from σύν and κρίνω; to judge of one thing in connection with another, i.e. combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance):--compare among (with).

G4770.d: from στοά; a "Stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), i.e. adherent of a certin philosophy:--Stoick.

G4878.d: from σύν and ἀντιλαμβάνομαι; to take hold of opposite together, i.e. co-operate (assist):--help.

G4552.d: of Hebrew origin (סַפִּיר); a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem:--sapphire.

G4626.d: apparently a primary verb; to dig:--dig.

G4595.d: apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. (figuratively) perish:--be corrupted.

G4976.d: from the alternate of ἔχω; a figure (as a mode or circumstance), i.e. (by implication) external condition:--fashion.

G4798.d: from σύν and χράομαι; to use jointly, i.e. (by implication) to hold intercourse in common:--have dealings with.

G4930.d: from συντελέω; entire completion, i.e. consummation (of a dispensation):--end.

G4783.d: from συγκατατίθεμαι; a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) accord with:--agreement.

G4961.d: from σύν and στρατιώτης; a co-campaigner, i.e. (figuratively) an associate in Christian toil:--fellowsoldier.

G4876.d: from σύν and a derivative of ἀντί; to meet with; figuratively, to occur:--befall, meet.

G4597.d: apparently of Hebrew origin (סָס); a moth:--moth.

G4670.d: plural of Hebrew origin (סְדֹם); Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine:--Sodom.

G4618.d: from a derivative of σῖτος; grain-fed, i.e. fattened:--fatted.

G4859.d: from σύν and φωνή; sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement):-- consent.

G4584.d: of Hebrew origin (שִׁמְעִי); Semei (i.e. Shimi), an Israelite:--Semei.

G4709.d: adverb from σπουδαῖος; earnestly, promptly:--diligently, instantly.

G4673.d: probably akin to the base of σωρεύω; a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier:--bier.

G4897.d: from σύν and εἰσέρχομαι; to enter in company with:--go in with, go with into.

G4619.d: from a derivative of σῖτος; grained, i.e. fatted:--fatling.

G4676.d: of Latin origin; a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse):--handkerchief, napkin.

G4905.d: from σύν and ἔρχομαι; to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally):--accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort.

G4533.d: of Hebrew origin (שַׂלְמוֹן); Salmon, an Israelite:--Salmon.

G4692.d: probably strengthened from πούς; to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly:--(make, with) haste unto.

G4634.d: from σκῆνος and πήγνυμι; the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes):--tabernacles.

G4588.d: of Latin origin; Sergius, a Roman:--Sergius.

G4899.d: from a compound of σύν and ἐκλέγομαι; chosen in company with, i.e. co-elect (fellow Christian):--elected together with.

G4935.d: adverb from a derivative of συντέμνω; concisely (briefly):--a few words.

G4722.d: from στέγη; to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently):--(for-)bear, suffer.

G4834.d: from συμπαθής; to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate:--have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.

G4641.d: feminine of a compound of σκληρός and καρδία; hard-heartedness, i.e. (specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception:--hardness of heart.

G4826.d: from the same as Σίμων; Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites:--Simeon, Simon.

G4640.d: akin to (to skip); to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus):--leap (for joy).

G4693.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a grotto); a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort:--cave, den.

G4536.d: perhaps from σάλος (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); a trumpet:--trump(-et).

G4553.d: apparently of Hebrew origin (שָׂרַג); a basket (as interwoven or wicker-work:--basket.

G4855.d: from σύν and φύω; passive, to grow jointly:--spring up with.

G4898.d: from σύν and the base of ἐκδημέω; a co-absentee from home, i.e. fellow-traveller:--companion in travel, travel with.

G4717.d: from σταυρός; to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness:--crucify.

G4813.d: from a derivative of (to strip; probably akin to αἱρέομαι; compare σκῦλον); to despoil:--rob.

G4502.d: of Hebrew origin (רְאוּבֵן); Ruben (i.e. Reuben), an Israelite:--Reuben.

G4669.d: from Σμύρνα; to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic):--mingle with myrrh.

G4816.d: from σύν and λέγω in its original sense; to collect:--gather (together, up).

G4983.d: from σώζω; the body (as a sound whole), used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively:--bodily, body, slave.

G4638.d: from σκηνόω; an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul):-- tabernacle.

G4539.d: probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from שָׁלוֹם); Salome (i.e. Shelomah), an Israelitess:--Salome.

G4612.d: of Latin origin; a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron):--apron.

G4959.d: from σύν and στενάζω; to moan jointly, i.e. (figuratively) experience a common calamity:--groan together.

G4757.d: from a presumed derivative of the same as στρατιά; a camper-out, i.e. a (common) warrior (literally or figuratively):--soldier.

G4925.d: from σύν and οἰκοδομέω; to construct, i.e. (passively) to compose (in company with other Christians, figuratively):--build together.

G4967.d: from σφάζω; butchery (of animals for food or sacrifice, or (figuratively) of men (destruction)):--slaughter.

G4769.d: from (to stiffen; properly akin to the base of ἵστημι); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support:--pillar.

G4902.d: middle voice from σύν and a primary (to follow); to attend (travel) in company with:--accompany.

G4837.d: from σύν and παρακαλέω; to console jointly:--comfort together.

G4870.d: from σύν and ἀκολουθέω; to accompany:--follow.

G4884.d: from σύν and ἁρπάζω; to snatch together, i.e. seize:--catch.

G4920.d: from σύν and (to send); to put together, i.e. (mentally) to comprehend; by implication, to act piously:-- consider, understand, be wise.

G4938.d: from συντρίβω; concussion or utter fracture (properly, concretely), i.e. complete ruin:--destruction.

G4767.d: from a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary (to hate); hated, i.e. odious:--hateful.

G4630.d: apparently of Latin origin; left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scævus), an Israelite:--Sceva.

G4886.d: from σύν and δεσμόν; a joint tie, i.e. ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control:--band, bond.

G4515.d: adverb from a presumed derivative of Ῥώμη; Romaistically, i.e. in the Latin language:--Latin.

G4937.d: from σύν and the base of τρίβος; to crush completely, i.e. to shatter (literally or figuratively):--break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise.

G4689.d: apparently a primary verb; to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend"):--(be ready to) be offered.

G4919.d: from σύν and (to crumble); to crush together, i.e. (figuratively) to dispirit:--break.

G4895.d: from σύν and εἰμί (including its various inflections); to be in company with, i.e. present at the time:--be with.

G4968.d: neuter of a derivative of σφαγή; a victim (in sacrifice):--slain beast.

G4801.d: from σύν and the base of ζεῦγος; to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage):--join together.

G4842.d: from σύν and πέμπω; to despatch in company:--send with.

G4838.d: from σύν and παραλαμβάνω; to take along in company:--take with.

G4844.d: from σύν and πίνω; to partake a beverage in company:--drink with.

G4780.d: from σύν and καλύπτω; to conceal altogether:--cover.

G4785.d: from σύν and a compound of κατά and ψηφίζω; to count down in company with, i.e. enroll among:--number with.

G4570.d: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish (literally or figuratively):--go out, quench.

G4629.d: from a derivative of (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of σκοπός through the idea of noticeableness); clothing:--raiment.

G4869.d: from σύν and αἰχμάλωτος; a co-captive:--fellowprisoner.

G4782.d: from σύν and καταβαίνω; to descend in company with:--go down with.

G4660.d: apparently a primary verb; to flay, i.e. (figuratively) to harass:--trouble(self).

G4973.d: probably strengthened from φράσσω; a signet (as fencing in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication, the stamp impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively:--seal.

G4567.d: of Chaldee origin corresponding to מַעְבָּד (with the definite affix); the accuser, i.e. the devil:--Satan.

G4805.d: from συζεύγνυμι; co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian:--yokefellow.

G4985.d: adverb from σωματικός; corporeally or physically:--bodily.

G4720.d: the same as στάχυς; Stachys, a Christian:--Stachys.

G4901.d: from σύν and ἐπιμαρτυρέω; to testify further jointly, i.e. unite in adding evidence:--also bear witness.

G4900.d: from σύν and ἐλαύνω; to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation):--+ set at one again.

G4590.d: of Hebrew origin (שֵׁם); Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch:-- Sem.

G4603.d: from σίδηρος; made of iron:--(of) iron.

G4663.d: of uncertain derivation; a grub, maggot or earth-worm:--worm.

G4962.d: from σύν and στρέφω; to twist together, i.e. collect (a bundle, a crowd):--gather.

G4625.d: ("scandal"); probably from a derivative of κάμπτω; a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin):--occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock.

G4531.d: from σάλος; to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite:--move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up.

G4858.d: from σύμφωνος; unison of sound ("symphony"), i.e. a concert of instruments (harmonious note):--music.

G4893.d: from a prolonged form of συνείδω; co-perception, i.e. moral consciousness:--conscience.

G4764.d: akin to στερεός; a "straining", "strenuousness" or "strength", i.e. (figuratively) luxury (voluptuousness):--delicacy.

G4659.d: from (sullen) and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance:--of a sad countenance.

G4788.d: from σύν and κλείω; to shut together, i.e. include or (figuratively) embrace in a common subjection to:--conclude, inclose, shut up.

G4679.d: from σοφός; to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error:--cunningly devised, make wise.

G4541.d: from Σαμάρεια; a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria:--Samaritan.

G4821.d: from σύν and βασιλεύω; to be co-regent (figuratively):--reign with.

G4929.d: from σύν and τάσσω; to arrange jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to direct:--appoint.

G4582.d: from (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι, through the idea of attractiveness); the moon:--moon.

G4620.d: from σῖτος and μέτρον; a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food):--portion of meat.

G4655.d: from the base of σκιά; shadiness, i.e. obscurity (literally or figuratively):--darkness.

G4564.d: of Hebrew origin (שָׂרָה); Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham:--Sara, Sarah.

G4656.d: from σκότος; to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively):--be full of darkness.

G4792.d: from σύν and κομίζω; to convey together, i.e. collect or bear away in company with others:--carry.

G4696.d: of uncertain derivation; a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace:--spot.

G4871.d: from σύν and (to throng); to accumulate, i.e. convene:--assemble together.

G4865.d: from σύν and ἀγωνίζομαι; to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant):--strive together with.

G4543.d: from Σάμος and (Thrace); Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean:--Samothracia.

G4796.d: from σύν and χαίρω; to sympathize in gladness, congratulate:--rejoice in (with).

G4652.d: from σκότος; opaque, i.e. (figuratively) benighted:--dark, full of darkness.

G4721.d: strengthened from a primary (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building); a roof:--roof.

G4580.d: of Latin origin; "second"; Secundus, a Christian:--Secundus.

G4840.d: from σύν and πάρειμι; to be at hand together, i.e. now present:--be here present with.

G4672.d: of Hebrew origin (שְׁלֹמֹה); Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David:--Solomon.

G4927.d: from σύν and a derivative of a compound of the base of 3674 and the base of ὅριον; to border together, i.e. adjoin:--join hard.

G4942.d: from σύν and ὑποκρίνομαι; to act hypocritically in concert with:--dissemble with.

G4568.d: of Hebrew origin (סְאָה); a certain measure for things dry:--measure.

G4882.d: from σύν and ἀποστέλλω; to despatch (on an errand) in company with:--send with.

G4738.d: from ἵστημι (as standing prominently); the (entire external) bosom, i.e. chest:--breast.

G4523.d: probably from Σαδώκ; a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite:--Sadducee.

G4765.d: diminutive of (a sparrow); a little sparrow:--sparrow.

G4825.d: from σύν and βουλή; a consultor, i.e. adviser:--counsellor.

G4742.d: from a primary (to "stick", i.e. prick); a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service:--mark.

G4851.d: from σύν and φέρω (including its alternate); to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage:--be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for).

G4999.d: plural of Latin origin; huts or wooden-walled buildings; Tabernæ:--taverns.

G4544.d: of uncertain affinity; Samus, an island of the Mediterranean:--Samos.

G4890.d: from (the alternate of) συντρέχω; a running together, i.e. (riotous) concourse:--run together.

G4940.d: from σύν and τυγχάνω; to chance together, i.e. meet with (reach):--come at.

G4574.d: from σεβάζομαι; something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc):--devotion, that is worshipped.

G4508.d: from ῥύπος; dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked:--vile.

G4762.d: strengthened from the base of τροπή; to twist, i.e. turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively):--convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about).

G4687.d: probably strengthened from σπάω (through the idea of extending); to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively):--sow(- er), receive seed.

G4594.d: neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article ὁ (t changed to s) and ἡμέρα; on the (i.e. this) day (or night current or just passed); generally, now (i.e. at present, hitherto):--this (to-)day.

G4818.d: from σύν and λυπέω; to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone:--be grieved.

G4924.d: from σύν and οἰκέω; to reside together (as a family):--dwell together.

G4598.d: from σής and a derivative of βιβρώσκω; moth-eaten:--motheaten.

G4511.d: from ῥύομαι in the sense of its congener ῥέω; a flux (of blood):--issue.

G4969.d: a primary verb; to butcher (especially an animal for food or in sacrifice) or (generally) to slaughter, or (specially), to maim (violently):--kill, slay, wound.

G4503.d: of Hebrew origin (רוּת); Ruth, a Moabitess:--Ruth.

G4522.d: from a derivative of (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); a "seine" for fishing:--net.

G4873.d: from σύν and ἀνακεῖμαι; to recline in company with (at a meal):--sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat).

G4563.d: from a derivative of (to brush off; akin to σύρω); meaning a broom; to sweep:--sweep.

G4561.d: probably from the base of σαρόω; flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specially), a human being (as such):--carnal(-ly, + -ly minded), flesh(-ly).

G4611.d: of Hebrew origin (שִׁלֹחַ); Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem:--Siloam.

G4946.d: plural of uncertain derivation; Syracuse, the capital of Sicily:--Syracuse.

G4843.d: from σύν and a compound of περί and λαμβάνω; to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. earnestly throw the arms about one:--embrace.

G4914.d: from a compound of σύν and ἦθος; mutual habituation, i.e. usage:--custom.

G4835.d: from συμπάσχω; having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative:--having compassion one of another.

G4787.d: from σπαράσσω and κινέω; to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition):--stir up.

G4569.d: of Hebrew origin, the same as Σαούλ; Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul:--Saul.

G4750.d: probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of τομώτερος; the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication, language (and its relations); figuratively, an opening (in the earth); specially, the front or edge (of a weapon):--edge, face, mouth.

G4848.d: from σύν and πορεύομαι; to journey together; by implication, to assemble:--go with, resort.

G4554.d: plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor:--Sardis.

G4639.d: apparently a primary word; "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)):-- shadow.

G4836.d: from σύν and παραγίνομαι; to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid:--come together, stand with.

G4781.d: from σύν and κάμπτω; to bend together, i.e. (figuratively) to afflict:--bow down.

G4918.d: from σύν and θλίβω; to compress, i.e. crowd on all sides:--throng.

G4549.d: of Hebrew origin (שָׁאוּל); Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul:--Saul. Compare Σαῦλος.

G4702.d: from σπόρος; sown, i.e. (neuter plural) a planted field:--corn(-field).

G4661.d: neuter from σκύλλω; something stripped (as a hide), i.e. booty:--spoil.

G4500.d: adverb from a derivative of (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. with a crash:--with a great noise.

G4713.d: from the base of ἵστημι (as stationary); a jar or earthen tank:--pot.

G4991.d: feminine of a derivative of σωτήρ as (properly, abstract) noun; rescue or safety (physically or morally):--deliver, health, salvation, save, saving.

G4810.d: apparently a primary word; a fig:--fig.

G4719.d: from the base of ἵστημι; a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk):--ear (of corn).

G4615.d: perhaps from (to hurt, i.e. sting); mustard (the plant):--mustard.

G4684.d: from (luxury); to be voluptuous:--live in pleasure, be wanton.

G4759.d: from στρατόπεδον and ἄρχω; a ruler of an army, i.e. (specially), a Prætorian præfect:--captain of the guard.

G4987.d: from another form of σορός; to pile up (literally or figuratively):--heap, load.

G4616.d: of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it):--(fine) linen (cloth).

G4648.d: from σκοπός; to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard:--consider, take heed, look at (on), mark. Compare ὀπτάνομαι.

G4688.d: of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman):--executioner.

G4562.d: of Hebrew origin (שְׂרוּג); Saruch (i.e. Serug), a patriarch:--Saruch.

G4647.d: perhaps from the base of σκέλος and ὀπτάνομαι; withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability):--thorn.

G4708.d: adverb from σπουδαιότερος; more speedily, i.e. sooner than otherwise:--more carefully.

G4812.d: from the base of συλάω and (the reduplicated form of) ἄγω; to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce:--spoil.

G4866.d: from σύν and ἀθλέω; to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly:--labour with, strive together for.

G4807.d: of Hebrew origin (שִׁקְמָה) in imitation of συκομωραία; a sycamore-fig tree:--sycamine tree.
